correctness.rationale: Schmidt probabilities λ1=(2d+1)/(3d), λ2..d=1/(3d) are positive and normalized. Kraus diagonals (1/√(2d+1),1,..,1) and (√(2d/(2d+1)),0,..,0) have squared sums I. Outcome one occurs with probability 1/3 and has all Schmidt probabilities 1/d; outcome two occurs with probability 2/3 and is product. Therefore average C_d=1/(3d^d) versus input (2d+1)/(3d)^d; exact factor 3^(d-1)/(2d+1)>1 for all d≥3 by induction, diverging exponentially. Independent exact-rational computations d=3,4,5,10,20 corroborate the algebra. This is strong average LOCC, not deterministic Nielsen majorization.
residual_risks: Pure bipartite systems of local dimension d≥3, raw unrooted top member only, not mixed-state extensions or lower hierarchy members.
